text:
alex: Heads-up — we've been asked by a couple of teams for better visibility into why the gateway chooses a specific model. They want an auditable trace for pinning/compat fallbacks, esp for customer incidents.

maria: +1. Product needs a clear timeline in the console: which rule matched, model alias resolved, and any compatibility-based downgrade. Important for rollouts and CS. :eyes:

sam: Agree on value, but we need to consider perf & PII. If we emit full decision traces on every request it could bloat logs and include tenant-level metadata. Two quick options: (1) sampling with full traces, (2) always emit compact header + sampled verbose events.

peggy: For the SDKs we could expose a single response header to consumers for debug mode, e.g. `X-Redwood-Routing-Decision`. That avoids needing app teams to peek into infra logs.

alex: I like header + sampled event. Proposal: always include a tiny header like `X-Redwood-Route-Trace: model=redwood-v2;rule=route-23;mode=pin` and send a full decision event to telemetry when `X-Debug-Route=1` request header or when sampled.

jordan: Telemetry notes: full decision event schema will be ~1KB per event. At 0.1% sampling that's ~1MB/day per 12.5k QPS — still significant across tenants. Need budgeted retention and a queryable store (Elastic/Clickhouse). We should also include a `trace_id` in header to join events.

sam: +1 on `trace_id`. Also, let's avoid including customer prompts in any of these events. Decision event should contain rule ids, model alias/version, compatibility flags, and reason codes only.

maria: Console UX: want a per-route history panel showing recent decisions (collapsed), and a pin audit view that shows who pinned, when, and what compatibility constraints were applied. Ideally link to telemetry traces for deep-dive.

peggy: For canary rollouts we want an event that ties decision -> rollout cohort. Suggest adding `cohort=canary-3` to the decision payload when applicable so console can filter by cohort.

alex: Implementation sketch: 

```
# header (always small)
X-Redwood-Route-Trace: model=redwood-v2,rule=route-23,trace=rt-2054321987-025

# example telemetry event (sampled or debug)
{
  "trace_id": "rt-2054321987-025",
  "route": "route-23",
  "rule_chain": ["expr:v2_compat","quota:tenantA","pin:alias-redwood-stable"],
  "resolved_model": "redwood-v2-3.1",
  "fallbacks": ["redwood-v2-3.0 (quantized)"] ,
  "reason_codes": ["incompatible-opt-ops","quota-exhausted"]
}
```

sam: A couple of security bits: ensure `trace_id` is ephemeral (TTL 7 days) and redact tenant identifiers unless the tenant consents. Also encrypt telemetry at rest with current KMS.

jordan: For rollout analytics, we'll want join keys: `trace_id`, `tenant_id` (hashed), `timestamp`, `cohort`. That will let product compute error/latency deltas by cohort.

maria: UX backlog item: (1) pin audit timeline, (2) route decision debug pane (with link to sampled traces), (3) toggle to turn on header emission for a workspace.

alex: Can infra team give rough estimate? Two parts: a) runtime change to emit header + trace_id (low), b) telemetry pipeline and retention + console UI (medium).

infra-bot: deployment queued: `route-trace/header-v1` -> canary on eng-platform tomorrow 09:00 UTC.

peggy: I'll own SDK opt-in: flag `enableRoutingDebugHeader` that sets `X-Debug-Route=1` on dev environments.

sam: I'll draft a privacy-safe event schema and a short checklist for security review.

maria: Thanks everyone — I'll file a product ticket with the UX mock and link to Sam's schema once ready. :+1:

devex-bot: Related doc: https://internal.redwood.dev/docs/routing-audit (draft)

alex: OK planning next steps: Sam -> schema draft by EOD, Infra -> perf estimate by EOD, Peggy -> SDK flag PR next week, Maria -> product ticket. We'll sync in tomorrow's eng-platform stand if any blockers.
